statement:
Patchboard manages reversible overlays on object attributes.

There are `N` objects and `K` permanently existing attribute cells. A cell stores either an integer (`I x`) or an object reference (`O x`).

A path consists of a root object and `L >= 1` attribute numbers. Starting at the root, read and follow the object reference in every attribute except the last; the last attribute identifies the target cell. Paths are resolved when used, against the current state.

Each activation now contains an ordered transaction of `M >= 1` replacements. On `START`, process its replacements from first to last. For each replacement, resolve its path after all preceding replacements in that same activation have been applied, remember the identified cell and its current value, then write the replacement value. After all replacements, append the activation ID to the global activation order. The ID is guaranteed inactive before `START`, but may be reused after stopping.

`STOP id` does nothing if `id` is inactive. Otherwise, restore that activation's remembered writes in reverse replacement order, then remove it from the global activation order. Each restoration writes the remembered value even if another activation later changed that cell. Remembered paths are never resolved again.

`STOPALL` stops all active activations from newest to oldest. Each complete restoration occurs before the next activation is stopped.

Input:
- First line: `N K Q`.
- Next `K` lines: `object attribute kind value`. Each `(object, attribute)` pair is unique.
- Next `Q` lines contain one command:
  - `START id M`, followed on the same line by `M` groups of `root L a1 ... aL kind value`
  - `STOP id`
  - `STOPALL`
  - `GET root L a1 ... aL`
  - `STACK`

`GET` resolves its path and prints its cell as `I x` or `O x`.

`STACK` prints the number of active activations followed by their IDs from oldest to newest on one line.

Object and activation IDs are positive integers; activation IDs are at most `Q`. Attributes are in `1..=10^9`. Integer values fit signed 64-bit integers. Every object reference, including replacements, is in `1..=N`. Every path has declared cells and object references at all intermediate positions at the exact moment it is resolved.

Constraints: `1 <= N,K,Q <= 200000`. Across all `START` commands, the total `M` is at most `200000`. The sum of all path lengths in all commands is at most `400000`. The total number of activation IDs printed by all `STACK` commands is at most `400000`.

Output only the requested lines. Tokens are compared after splitting on ASCII whitespace bytes `0x09..0x0D` and `0x20`.

Submit one complete Rust program using only the standard library and containing `fn main()`. It must use stdin and stdout only, with no filesystem, network, external crates, unsafe code, or nondeterminism.
